title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

reports.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

summary:
Former Costa Mesa police officer Robert Jay Josett, 35, pleaded guilty to three misdemeanors after harassing a former mistress and misusing police databases. After she ended the relationship in April 2024, he contacted her thousands of times by text, phone, and social media over nine months, sometimes more than 100 times in one day, and called her and her new boyfriend up to 58 times in a single day. He also made 13 unauthorized searches in the California Law Enforcement Telecommunications System on his mistress, someone she dated, and his wife, and used the police department's license plate reader system to track vehicles, including after he was placed on leave.

Josett was served with an emergency protective order and notice of termination on June 28, 2024, then drove by the woman's home and was arrested. He was sentenced to three years informal probation and a 52-week domestic violence program, and he had already spent nine months on a GPS ankle monitor. His law enforcement certification review by Peace Officers Standards and Training is pending.
